# Returns and Complaints Resolution Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Returns and Complaints Resolution Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved service environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded case documents, proposed CRM, ERP, SharePoint and Teams access and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the read-only CRM case feed, order and policy evidence and the authorized resolution workflow. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare customer service, quality, loss-prevention and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer. | Customer or partner |
| Write controls | Plan authenticated tools, explicit human approval, authorization checks and audit logging for any production write; the workshop performs no writes. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service operations owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Return and complaint review consistency, handling effort and the policy evidence used today. Show where fragmented policy, product and service context slows or varies decisions before agreeing success measures.

Fill your baseline record:

| Case type | Measurement period | Case volume | Review effort | Policy source | Escalations | Review owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree service replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service operations owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Service operations owner | Approve policy sources, audience and success measures; keep synthetic case values and trends out of customer results. |
| Authorized service, quality and loss-prevention reviewers | Decide returns, refunds, credits, exchanges and customer messages through separate approved tooling; keep pattern review non-accusatory. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before approving any service connection. |
| CRM, ERP and policy connection owners | Approve read-only case, order and policy connections and the resolution workflow's authentication, authorization and audit controls. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check RCR-01 through RCR-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject missing anchors and reshoot-required captures. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route case decisions to authorized reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Service replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The service owner records how returns and complaints are reviewed today and where policy, product or service context is fragmented.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/returns-complaints-resolution/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The administrator's data policies cover the proposed CRM, ERP, SharePoint and Teams connectors, knowledge sources and intended channel; blocked routes stay blocked.
- [ ] The customer confirms authenticated audience and least-privilege access for customer case and order data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/returns-complaints-resolution/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/returns-complaints-resolution/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/returns-complaints-resolution/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/returns-complaints-resolution/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Returns and Complaints Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_returns-complaints-rules-and-safety.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_returns-complaints-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: complaint-classification
9. Add skill: resolution-recommendation
10. Add skill: return-processing
11. Add skill: trend-analysis
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass RCR-01: Customer Service Agent
15. Pass RCR-02: Customer Service Agent
16. Pass RCR-03: Customer Service Agent
17. Pass RCR-04: Quality Team
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: RCR-01, RCR-02, RCR-03, RCR-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `ReturnsComplaintsResolutionAgent` and returns `Draft Return Review Queue` and `no return`.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged RCR prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges every case on its final response; annotated screenshots are checkpoints, not the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing customer case or order data. Request only the read scopes needed for approved case, order and policy sources. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 CRM and ERP

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** CRM, ERP and policy connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 CRM and ERP — read:** Add approved read-only case and order connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 CRM and ERP:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 CRM and ERP:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 CRM and ERP:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Query no live system and change no case; use only the uploaded synthetic records. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, refund, return or message succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate SharePoint governed policy knowledge

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** CRM, ERP and policy connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint governed policy knowledge — read:** Add approved SharePoint policy content as knowledge with a content owner.

2. **Identity for SharePoint governed policy knowledge:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint governed policy knowledge:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint governed policy knowledge:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Accuse no one; describe aggregate patterns for loss-prevention review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, refund, return or message succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Authorized service resolution workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** CRM, ERP and policy connection owners

1. **Bind Authorized service resolution workflow — write:** Require authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit approval and audit logging before any write (preview).

2. **Identity for Authorized service resolution workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Authorized service resolution workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Authorized service resolution workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Process no refund and send no message; state that no external side effect occurred. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, refund, return or message succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** CRM, ERP and policy connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — write:** Keep drafts unsent until an approved workflow posts them.

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Accuse no one; describe aggregate patterns for loss-prevention review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, refund, return or message succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** CRM, ERP and policy connection owners

Bind only approved read-only connections and keep every write action in the separate authorized workflow.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no lookup or update is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] Any write runs only through authenticated tools with authorization checks, explicit human approval and audit logging.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as intended reviewers and an unshared identity; a maker's access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic volumes, rates and refund totals are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked returns corpus | All four cases, RCR-01 through RCR-04, include every required anchor. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Service authority boundary | Any return, refund, credit, replacement, shipment, reservation, account change or customer message is no-go. |
| Privacy and non-accusation | Echoed personal or sensitive text, or an accusation against an individual, is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required captures. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service operations owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service operations owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved service audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Service operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Step 6-5. Operate

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review failed case sessions, echoed personal text, connection errors and credit consumption in Monitor.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
